interest: This collection is particularly valuable for historians examining the complex interplay of intelligence, covert operations, and great-power diplomacy in French Indochina during World War II. The documents illuminate how Japanese entities—such as Domei News Agency correspondents and formal liaison headquarters with the Vichy administration—functioned as covers for espionage and subversive activities aimed at undermining French colonial authority. Furthermore, the high-level memoranda of conversation between Secretary of State Stettinius and British Ambassador Lord Halifax provide critical insight into British efforts under Lord Mountbatten's South East Asia Command (SEAC) to sponsor French sabotage networks, underscoring President Roosevelt's personal oversight and reluctance to sanction Allied operations that might compromise postwar policy regarding Indochina.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.20251G, File 1479) documents intelligence, espionage, and covert military activities involving Japan and Allied countermeasures in French Indochina between March 1941 and December 1944. The file begins with early wartime cross-reference sheets concerning Japanese subversive efforts—specifically a Domei News Agency representative acting as an undercover agent—and intercepted radio communications transmitted by J. Edgar Hoover's Department of Justice. The remainder of the file comprises a secret November 1944 Office of Strategic Services (OSS) memorandum identifying the relocation of the Japanese espionage and liaison headquarters in Indochina from Hué to Tourane (Da Nang), as well as two December 1944 memoranda of conversation between Secretary of State Edward R. Stettinius, Jr., and British Ambassador Lord Halifax regarding Lord Mountbatten's proposal to deploy French personnel for sabotage operations in Indochina, a matter held for the personal decision of President Franklin D. Roosevelt.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a military attaché report regarding a Domei News Agency representative in French Indochina suspected of conducting subversive activities for Japan.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes an original report (No. 39) dated March 18, 1941, sent by Military Attaché O'Rear. It details allegations that a Domei News representative in Indochina identified as 'Ata (?)' was acting as a direct Japanese operative. The agent was reportedly engaged in subversive activities designed to weaken French authority and lay the groundwork for Japanese military intervention.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Domei News Representative in Indo-China

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording the Department of Justice's transmission of intercepted radio messages and translations concerning Japanese activities.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet references a letter dated March 24, 1942, from J. Edgar Hoover of the Department of Justice. The communication transmitted copies and translations of intercepted radio messages relating to Japanese intelligence and operations. The underlying material was catalogued under State Department classification 862.20294/42.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Intercepted Japanese Radio Messages

subfiles.about: Secret OSS intelligence memorandum reporting the transfer of the Japanese Liaison Headquarters and espionage base in French Indochina from Hué to Tourane.
subfiles.from: Bernard A. Towell (Office of Strategic Services)
subfiles.summary: Bernard A. Towell of the Office of Strategic Services (I-2 Branch) informs Jack D. Neal of the Department of State regarding intelligence obtained on September 22, 1944, from a source evaluated A-2. The report revealed that the Japanese Liaison Headquarters with the Vichy French authorities had moved from Hué to Tourane (Da Nang). The memorandum emphasizes that this liaison bureau functioned primarily as a cover for Japanese espionage operations, and notes that the information had not been distributed to U.S. embassies abroad.
subfiles.title: OSS Memorandum on Japanese Espionage Headquarters in French Indo-China

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation between Secretary of State Stettinius and British Ambassador Lord Halifax concerning British inquiries on sabotage activities in French Indochina.
subfiles.from: Edward R. Stettinius, Jr. (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Edward R. Stettinius, Jr., records a discussion held on the morning of December 8, 1944, with British Ambassador Lord Halifax. Halifax inquired about the status of a pending British communication regarding sabotage activities in French Indochina that had not yet received an American reply. Stressing the urgency of the issue, Halifax received assurances from Stettinius that the State Department would provide an answer within the coming week.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Stettinius and Halifax on Sabotage in French Indo-China

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation detailing British requests for presidential approval to attach French personnel to Lord Mountbatten's headquarters for sabotage operations in Indochina.
subfiles.from: Edward R. Stettinius, Jr. (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Stettinius details a conference with Lord Halifax following up on a proposal first raised on November 23 regarding Lord Mountbatten attaching French personnel to his South East Asia Command headquarters for sabotage in French Indochina. After consulting with H. Freeman Matthews, Stettinius informed Halifax that the proposal was currently before President Franklin D. Roosevelt awaiting his decision. Lord Halifax urged Stettinius to personally raise the matter with the President during their next meeting due to the high importance Mountbatten placed on executing the operation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Stettinius and Halifax on Mountbatten's Sabotage Operations in Indo-China
